universalAnswers.whatHappened: Anthropic and OpenAI published internal measurements showing greater use of AI agents in frontier-lab research.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: Measurements of supervised research work inside two AI companies, not a consumer feature launch.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: Two primary provider reports with methods and limitations.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Self-reported internal measurements with different methods; no independent cross-lab comparison.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: The numbers are evidence of changed research practice, not proof of autonomous recursive self-improvement.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: Frontier-lab researchers directly; the public indirectly through the pace and governance of model development.
universalAnswers.changesNow: Agents perform more bounded research work and longer tasks under human direction.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Overall research acceleration, cross-lab comparability and independent verification remain unresolved.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Ask what work was counted, what humans still decide and who checked the measure.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Which decision rights remain human as task execution becomes more automated?

research-benchmark.researchQuestion: How much defined research work are agents performing inside Anthropic and OpenAI, and how much human involvement remains?
research-benchmark.method: Anthropic built a prototype internal automation index with a Claude judge; OpenAI combined internal task estimates, interventions and agent runtime across its research organization.
research-benchmark.result: Anthropic reports Claude led 26% of measured research work, performed at least collaboratively in more than 90%, and was fully autonomous in none; OpenAI reports 3.1 eight-hour agent runtime units per human workday by mid-August.
research-benchmark.sponsorAndInterests: Each company performed and published its own measurement of systems it develops and uses.
research-benchmark.independentReplication: Neither supplied source provides independent replication or a common cross-company measurement method.
research-benchmark.realWorldTransfer: The measurements describe internal lab practice and do not establish a change to an everyday ChatGPT or Claude account or an overall productivity multiplier.
research-benchmark.limitations: Anthropic reports judge disagreement and no common cross-company method; OpenAI reports incomplete coverage and says runtime, code and experiment counts do not directly measure overall research progress.

translation.newsVersionExact: Two companies report different internal snapshots.
translation.actualMeaningExact: These figures describe work inside the companies that made the systems. They are not a change to an everyday ChatGPT or Claude account.
translation.mechanismExact: OpenAI says people still set priorities, judge results and decide whether to scale, pause or deploy.
translation.familiarExampleExact: Bounded investigations can run for hours, which may speed up a lab without transferring authority over the next model, evidence or deployment.

jargon.plainMeaning: Fully autonomous work removes the human
a model independently building its successor without a human in the loop

learningConnections.learningPayoff: See why giving an agent more of a task does not remove the human responsibility to define success and judge the result.
